confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from five web searches, which returned Numbeo Chania (inexpensive meal about EUR 15, cappuccino about EUR 3.6, domestic draft beer about EUR 4, mid-range meal for two about EUR 50), Crete Direct and Elxis 2026 guides, and Expatistan. The Numbeo figures were read from search-result summaries, not from the pages themselves. I converted EUR to USD at an assumed rate of about 1.16 USD per EUR from general knowledge, not from a search. Summer 2026 prices appear to be rising and harbour-front venues cost noticeably more than the local average, so I set anchors slightly above Numbeo averages for a July visit. Cocktail and wine are less certain. The cocktail comes from the Expatistan club average of EUR 9 and a harbour guide range of EUR 9-13. The wine glass is a house-wine estimate of about EUR 5-6 in a typical restaurant, against harbour prices of EUR 7-10 and a taverna beer of EUR 4-4.5. All four accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge of July peak-season Chania, with no accommodation searches and no live listings inspected. Hostel supply in Chania is thin, so the hostel figures are the least certain. The FX figure is the RBA representative AUD/USD rate of 0.6720 for 2026-11-18, taken from a search of the RBA exchange-rates page.
comparable_city_reasoning: Chania is a tourist-heavy Cretan city with prices close to the Greek average, but with a summer and harbour premium. I used Numbeo Chania as the main anchor and nudged it up for July peak season. Accommodation is benchmarked loosely against other peak-season Greek island and Mediterranean resort towns such as Rethymno, Heraklion and Corfu Town.
